subject.name: Dana Whitfield
subject.accounts_source: hw_identities.wm_ids — the binding ladder tier 4 actually matches on
subject.scope_note: 1 Weedmaps account(s) are bound to this person. Weedmaps lets one person sign up repeatedly under different emails, so reading only the account that placed an order under-reports what they bought.

state_reason: Dana Whitfield bought 2 products across 1 order on 1 bound Weedmaps account(s).
purchase_definition: A purchase here is an order Weedmaps sent us a Create webhook for (`pending`) whose status is not a cancellation. It does NOT mean delivered: no order in this database carries status COMPLETE, so defining it that way would report 'nothing bought' for every customer. `counts.stages` is the breakdown.

window.note: the timestamp of the Weedmaps Create webhook — when the order was placed, not when it was handed over

ranking_input.basis_sentence: Suggested from what this customer buys: 1 order, mostly Edibles. No product was bought twice, so this is a category match, not a repeat.
ranking_input.basis_contract: Render `basis_sentence` verbatim next to the suggestions. A ranking from history and a ranking from the house-brand default must never render identically; `basis_is_default` is the flag that decides which one the operator is looking at.

house_brand_default.basis: the owner's stated rule — first-timers gravitate to the house brand. This is a business rule, not a fact measured from this customer's behaviour.
house_brand_default.unbranded_note: 31 of the 31 catalogue products carry no brand_name at all. They are neither house brand nor another brand, so a house-brand-only ranking cannot see them; that is a coverage limit, not an empty result.

coverage.note: a product with no category cannot be ranked by category affinity and a product with no brand cannot be ranked by brand affinity. These counts are what a ranking actually covers; they are not zero-filled.

persona.reason: There is no persona or cohort model in this estate, and nothing here estimates one. A persona built from what is available today would be a guess presented as a segmentation.
would_need: A cohort definition somebody owns — what makes two customers 'similar' is a business decision (spend band? category mix? visit cadence? region?), not something to infer from a table.

Purchase history for enough customers to make a cohort mean anything. It exists: this module reads it. Nobody has ever aggregated it across people, and the aggregate is a second, larger read than this one.
A rule for the 33-of-149 unbranded and the uncategorised products, which would otherwise fall out of every cohort silently and make each cohort look tidier than it is.

A decision about cancelled orders and draft-only carts in a cohort — this module excludes both from purchases, and a cohort model that quietly includes them would disagree with this route about the same customer.

An honest label on the output: a cohort suggestion is not a personal one, and the UI contract in `ranking_input` (basis_is_default, basis_sentence) would need a third value rather than borrowing either existing one.
persona.next_task: PERSONA COHORTS — define the cohort key with the owner first, then aggregate this route across customers. Do not approximate it from a single customer's history.
